column2: Mean-squared displacement of an individual tracked organism
column3: Displacement of one cell_id centroid per MCS
column12: The conventional choice, and the one the earlier plan assumed. A cell_id is a computational biomass parcel, not an observable bacterium, so a per-cell MSD and a parcel MSD are not the same quantity. Usable only if a declared mapping from tracked cells to parcels is added.

column2: Decay rate of the spatial biomass autocorrelation
column3: Change in correlation length of the occupancy field per MCS
column4: Correlation length of the segmented biomass field over time
column12: SELECTED 2026-08-14. Field-level on BOTH sides, so it needs no cell-to-parcel mapping — which is what disqualified single-cell MSD. structure.correlation_length already computes the model side. dt_MCS = tau_exp / tau_sim from the decay of the normalised biomass field correlation, C_B(dt) = <dB(x,t) dB(x,t+dt)> / <dB(x,t)^2>. Selecting now rather than after spatial calibration is deliberate: it makes TIME-RESOLVED stacks a requirement of the campaign, avoiding a static campaign that would have to be repeated.

column4: Centroid motion of segmented aggregates between frames
column12: Aggregates are parcel-scale rather than cell-scale, so the semantics match. Requires aggregate identity to persist between frames, which segmentation alone does not guarantee.

column2: Rate of change of the biomass-void interface
column3: Change in specific interface area per MCS
column4: Change in measured interface area over time
column12: RUNNER-UP. Directly driven by the adhesion and volume terms, which is what the CPM's dynamics actually are, and structure.specific_interface_area computes the model side. Held in reserve because it is sensitive to the occupancy threshold, so it inherits whatever bias the declared occupancy mapping carries.

column2: Radial drift under a controlled gradient
column3: Change in the radial biomass profile per MCS
column4: Radial profile change under an imposed gradient
column12: Requires an experimental gradient that the CPM also represents. The nutrient field is written but never read by compute_delta_H, so today the model has no gradient response to match.

column2: Rate of increase of biofilm thickness
column12: EXCLUDED. Dominated by growth, and the CPM has no nutrient-driven biomass creation: divide_cell! has no trigger and state.nutrient is never read by compute_delta_H. No quantity of thickening data can calibrate a model that cannot thicken.

column2: Population or biomass specific growth rate
column4: Growth rate from OD or biovolume over time
column12: EXCLUDED for two independent reasons: the model has no growth, and a parcel count is not a cell count.
